Hitpoints XP comes from damage dealt (about 1.33 XP per point), so I trained Strength as high as I could and then hunted higher-HP targets.

- **Levelling:** Men, then cows, in Lumbridge took Strength to about 80 and Hitpoints to about 65 in roughly 20 minutes. That gave ~80–90 XP/min on cows.
- **Peak:** The 124 XP/min came from fighting Al-Kharid warriors, which have 19 HP and so waste less damage per kill. I paid the 10-coin toll with coins looted from goblins.
- **Setbacks:** I died to the warriors once early on. I died again during the peak fight, then couldn't cross the toll gate again in the last minutes.

My peak Thieving rate was **983 XP/min** (real-game normalized), in the 15-second window at 26m15s–26m30s. With about 45 seconds left there's no time for another run.

- **Levels 1–40:** I pickpocketed Lumbridge men. The first attempts stalled because the man kept attacking me. Once I sent pickpocket commands in a fast loop the rate climbed, and the peak was 84 XP/min before I moved on.
- **Levels 40–59:** I moved to the Varrock west guards, which give about 6 times the XP per success. HP was the limit, because each failed pick costs 2 HP and I had no food. The peak rose to 421 XP/min.
- **Death detour:** A `walkTo` toward Ardougne routed me through White Wolf Mountain, where I died. I lost my starting items and returned to Lumbridge.
- **Kebabs:** I paid the 10gp toll into Al Kharid and bought 22 kebabs for 1gp each. Back at the Varrock guards, I ate one whenever HP dropped to 7 or below. That loop made 563 pickpocket attempts, took Thieving from 59 to 82, and produced the 983 peak.
- **Ending:** I ran out of kebabs near the end and died again. Death doesn't remove XP, so the score is unaffected.

I wasn't able to test a bigger food stockpile, which is the likeliest way to score higher.
